comments.body:
My recommendation: prioritize faster complete runs and fewer unnecessary waits before a language rewrite. Keep this umbrella as an index to the existing owners.

**Most promising, in order**
1. **#1114: prove parallel macOS qualification.** This remains the strongest whole-run opportunity. First establish a same-commit, same-runner-class comparison with identical executed inventory and zero rescued failures. Choose a worker count supported by the actual runner; a six-worker Linux result is not a macOS capacity measurement.
2. **#1127: reduce how often full qualification is required, plus event coalescing.** This is missing from the checklist. Faster execution and fewer repeated executions solve different parts of the wait. Measure queue time, execution time, publication time and total operator wait separately. Keep one publication writer and preserve every landing's bookkeeping. A failed earlier attempt is not redundant successful evidence. Promotion-only qualification remains a separate, unapproved policy decision with delayed regression-detection risk.
3. **Bounded slow-suite improvements.** Start with stable, minimal ledger fixtures for gh549 and repeated setup/subprocess costs in gh436, once profiles confirm them. Preserve cases and isolation; sharing mutable fixtures can trade speed for intermittent failures. The marathon-audit optimization and fixed heavy-first ordering have already landed in #1123 (Oct 17, 8:23 PM PDT), so rebaseline before counting their savings again.

**Corrections and missing safeguards**
- The 67.7-minute macOS / 609-second Linux comparison is not an A/B result. It changes platform, runner resources, commit and coverage: the canary explicitly skips acorn-extract and pdda-repo-contract in validate.sh, and finishes red. acorn-extract also has a separate step, but that does not make the qualifying inventories identical. Useful directional evidence, not a measured ~6.7x qualifying improvement or proof that scheduling explains all the difference.
- The under-four-core fallback is **automatic-mode only**: [validate.sh at current development](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/655bc340b9e64056645a75f340e842c79371df3f/validate.sh#L976-L1015) applies it when no worker count was provided. An explicit --parallel N bypasses it; that permits an experiment, not a promise that oversubscription is beneficial.
- [Sequential shards](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/blob/655bc340b9e64056645a75f340e842c79371df3f/utils/py/wave_reconcile.py#L481-L528) are worth evaluating, but “sequential inside each shard” does not automatically satisfy today's full sequential receipt contract. Require an explicit reviewed aggregation contract: exact candidate/environment, complete union, no missing/duplicate suites, non-shell lanes, no rescued failure, fail-closed missing/cancelled shard, and one final publisher. Compare total runner-minutes as well as wall time.
- Add **#1126 deterministic failure diagnosis and process cleanup**. Preventing one environment-sensitive assertion from consuming another full run may matter more than shaving seconds from startup. Before proposing a rerun, report the exact test, severity, user impact, prior local result, cheapest focused reproduction and expected full-run wait. A focused pass diagnoses a failure; it does not replace release qualification.
- Treat bytecode caching as a small reversible measurement first. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE disables writes, not reads of existing valid caches; PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX redirects reads too, so it can introduce a cold-cache cost. Direct script execution and python -m also differ. Measure cold/warm cost and invocation counts before attributing minutes to recompilation ([Python documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.pycache_prefix)). Thin entry-point refactors follow only if measured savings justify their wider compatibility surface. Avoid a Rust/pytest rewrite without evidence that it changes the dominant cost.
- The test freeze is per new test/case/assertion/parameter, not merely per new suite or registry entry. “Edit an existing suite” is not blanket approval to add cases or alter policy.
- Keep estimates explicitly provisional. Rank remaining payoff against implementation/review time and extra CI runs; do not add overlapping savings. Record current/landed/parked status alongside each item.

Smallest useful next step: refresh the baseline after #1123, then complete #1114's bounded macOS proof under its existing owner. Keep #1127's cadence decision separate, and use #1118 for the comparison rather than creating another ranking system.

— dot

comments.body:
## Proposed current plan — October 17, 2026
Consolidates [review of this umbrella](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1130#issuecomment-6245419163) and the #1127 mitigation/prior-spike discussion.

**Authorization:** Noel has authorized a fresh, isolated **#836 technical spike and documentation of its results**. The broader sequence below remains proposed. No live CI-policy change, qualification relaxation, merge, deployment or new CI test/case/parameter is authorized by this plan.

### 1. Establish the new baseline and keep one owner per effort
- Start from current development, including merged #1123. Its marathon-audit optimization and fixed heavy-first ordering are already delivered; do not count them again as future savings.
- Use #1118's existing decisions/evidence as the comparison baseline, #1130 as the index, and the owning issues for results. Record delivered, remaining, parked and rejected work separately.
- Separate queue wait, test execution, publication and total operator wait. Report runner-minutes, first-attempt failures, rescues/skips and review/implementation cost as well as speed.
- Linux canary timing is directional evidence only: different hardware, code and documented exclusions prevent treating it as a controlled macOS qualification comparison.

### 2. Execute the bounded #836 hotspot spike now
Use /start-task in a fresh full clone on the Mac Studio, after checking for overlapping work.
1. Read #836/#835, the current code and existing evidence. Confirm which original hotspots still exist after intervening changes.
2. Measure the existing gh549 race/backfill and board-reconcile setup, plus gh436's duplicate parity execution. Establish paired same-machine, same-base timings and unchanged behavior.
3. Try the smallest isolated edits: use the minimum fixture data that still exercises the existing race and assertions; avoid re-running the same behavioral tests solely through the parity guard while retaining missing-reference validation and normal behavioral coverage.
4. Preserve independent fixture state, actual concurrency, outputs/exit semantics and existing failure-detection controls. Do not replace a real race with a serial mock or merely weaken an assertion.
5. Use existing focused checks first, retaining before/after logs, command/environment identity, elapsed times, failures and temporary negative-control results. No new permanent CI cases without per-case operator approval.
6. Document results on #836: measured savings versus variance, exact changes, coverage retained, limitations, reproduction steps and CONTINUE/PIVOT/PARK recommendation. A focused spike is not full release qualification. Propose any later full-gate comparison with its expected cost before spending another hour.
Keep tier reclassification, in-process rewrites, shared mutable fixture frameworks and unrelated fixes outside this spike. If current code has already fixed a target, record that prior art instead of rebuilding it.

### 3. Reliability and complete-run parallelism
- #1126: stabilize precise timeout-diagnosis assertions using controlled inputs while preserving real process termination/cleanup checks. A later green alone does not resolve the brittle assertion.
- #1114: finish the agreed bounded parallel proof with identical inventory on the same commit, zero rescued failures, and suitable hosted macOS evidence. Preserve serialized lanes and truthful receipt validation.
- The fewer-than-four-core fallback is automatic-mode only; an explicit worker count can be measured on the actual runner. Do not assume the Linux pool width is suitable for macOS.
- Sequential shards remain an alternative to investigate, not a loophole in today's single-run receipt rule. They require reviewed complete/disjoint inventory aggregation, exact identity, missing/cancelled-shard rejection and one final publisher.

### 4. Reassess #1127 after the cheaper fixes
The policy risk is delayed discovery of cross-feature regressions. Smaller checks cannot eliminate it.
Before reducing routine development coverage:
- Establish a genuinely blocking full-test checkpoint before promotion; the present main job runs after the push.
- Keep meaningful changed-area/dependency checks; shared infrastructure or uncertain classification requires broader review/checking.
- Use small, frequent promotion batches and bind evidence to the exact combined candidate. Changed code/base invalidates the applicable result.
- Keep targeted and full results distinct, preserve catch-up/bookkeeping, and verify cutover and rollback.
- Measure failures first discovered at promotion and the resulting diagnosis cost.
- Consider event coalescing separately: faster runs and fewer unnecessary runs address different costs, while failed attempts cannot be reused as passing evidence.

**Evidence gap:** #1076/#1079 demonstrated selective checks and receipt reuse locally, but no live optimized landing or stable-main qualification; that approach was parked. #1114 demonstrated local parallel speedups. Neither proves #1127's complete promotion-only process. If the remaining wait warrants #1127, first demonstrate its checkpoint, evidence handling and rollback on an isolated candidate without changing live policy.

### 5. Lower-priority experiments and stop conditions
- Bytecode caching: first measure cold/warm behavior and invocation counts; disabling bytecode writes does not disable existing-cache reads. Thin launchers follow only if measured payoff justifies product changes.
- Dynamic duration ordering must beat the heavy-first baseline already landed, preserve serialized lanes and have a deterministic fallback.
- Park a Rust/pytest rewrite until measured dominant costs justify it. Do not retire coverage merely to improve timing.
- Stop or park changes whose benefit disappears into measurement noise, whose setup/review cost exceeds likely savings, or which require weakening coverage. Do not multiply overlapping estimates.

### Failure communication before another expensive run
Report the exact failing test and what it protects, severity and practical impact, confidence in the diagnosis, recent/local results, the cheapest focused reproduction, and the expected full-run wait. Distinguish an automatically queued run from a proposed rerun. A local focused pass is diagnostic evidence, not a substitute for qualification.

— dot
